subject: Careers
title: Communication and asking for help
objective_verbatim: I can ask for clarification, report a problem or speak to a customer/colleague using appropriate language.
outcomes_verbatim: I can ask for clarification, report a problem or speak to a customer/colleague using appropriate language.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 2 Week 3, 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-12. Tuesday 9 March 2027, Tuesday P3. One 40-minute lesson. Spring 2 runs 22 February to Thursday 25 March 2027. Week 5 is four days with no Friday; the Tuesday lesson is unaffected.

outcomes_verbatim: I can ask for clarification, report a problem or speak to a customer/colleague using appropriate language.
sources.note: The current brief supplies the exact focuses, outcomes and row mapping. Other scheme columns are not asserted verbatim. Activities and 40-minute sequencing are newly authored in the accepted Spring 1 format.
Read for file shape, timing, tiers, feedback, private response and typed/scribed access conventions.
Read for the six-outcome closing Evidence Sheet grid pattern. Current six outcomes are rows 22–27 and current Week 5 combines rows 26–27.

source_adaptation: Exact owner-supplied focus and outcomes retained. Rows 26 and 27 share the closing Week 5 lesson. Newly authored invented workplace practice, not a quotation of absent sequence/evidence columns.
timing: Show the three words ASK, TELL and HELP. Read the goal aloud. Let pupils point, say or write one word. Explain that each made-up scene is in an unnamed workplace. Pupils may watch a model instead of acting. Read: 'A worker hears: Put it over there.' Ask what the worker needs to know. Accept a short question or a point to the unclear words. Say that asking a question can help work go well.

Model the worked example. Say the need, ask one short question, listen, then say the next step back. Model a calm tone without demanding eye contact. Show the difference between guessing and checking. Check for understanding: Which words ask where the items go?

Use scenarios 1 and 2. Build one question and one problem report as a group. Write the exact pupil words. Model the lead worker's reply, then invite one pupil to say the safe next step. Pupils can use a voice, a card or a short book response. Use the hinge. Every pupil chooses A, B or C before discussion. If all choose B and explain that it checks the task, move on. If any pupil chooses another answer, model 'Which box do you mean?' and check again with the parallel hinge. Keep all liquids and tools as paper scenes.

Offer Supported, Independent or Aspire cards. Pupils work in books. They may say answers for an adult to note. Keep the key goal the same across tiers. Do not require a pupil to act as a difficult customer. Use scenarios 3 and 4 for transfer. Use three brief response trials: ask for clarification, report a problem, and reply to a customer or colleague. Record the actual response and prompts for each trial.

Ask pupils to check one message: Is it kind? Is it clear? Does it say what is needed? Give one specific verbal feedback point and one next step. Invite a small edit. Do not equate a loud voice or eye contact with good communication. Read the exit scene. Accept one appropriate question. Ask the pupil to name who could help. Record the route, support and next step on the Evidence Sheet. Offer evidence to the Communication portfolio.
timing_basis: Accepted Spring 1 Careers format: 5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40. Processing time and short pauses sit inside the total. Slides marked same task time share the 12-minute independent block.

routes.Supported: Choose words from the bank. Say or copy one question. Complete one report with what and where. Choose a kind reply for the customer. Words: tray · box · spill · door · shelf Start: Which ___ do you mean? There is ___ by ___. Please can you help? I am not sure. I will ask for help.
routes.Independent: In your book, write a question for scene 1. Write a report for scene 2. Say what and where. Write a kind reply for scene 3. Read one reply back and check it.
routes.Aspire: Complete the three Independent messages. Use scene 4. Write a clear reply to the colleague. Explain how a question can help keep work safe. Improve one reply after feedback.

cases.title: Scene 1
cases.situation: A lead worker says, 'Put these cups on a tray.' There are two trays.
cases.question: What could the worker ask?
cases.reason: The question checks the task before the worker starts.

cases.title: Scene 2
cases.situation: A worker sees a spill by the door. People may slip.
cases.question: What could the worker do and say?
cases.answer: Keep clear and tell the lead worker: 'There is a spill by the door. Please can you help?'
cases.reason: The report says what is wrong and where it is. The worker asks the right person for help.

cases.title: Scene 3
cases.situation: A customer asks where the bags are. The worker does not know.
cases.question: What could the worker say?
cases.answer: I am not sure. I will ask someone who can help.
cases.reason: The reply is honest, kind and helpful.

cases.title: Scene 4
cases.situation: A colleague asks the worker to fetch a box. The worker did not hear which box.
cases.question: What could the worker say?
cases.answer: Please can you say which box you need?
cases.reason: The worker checks the detail without blaming the other person.

worked_example_and_fade.scene: A worker has to sort cups. They do not know which tray to use.
worked_example_and_fade.model: Pause and face the task. Ask: 'Which tray do you mean?' Listen or watch the lead worker show the tray. Check: 'So these cups go on this tray. Is that right?'
worked_example_and_fade.thinking: I do not need to guess. One clear question can help me start.
worked_example_and_fade.fade: Change the model to boxes on a shelf. Pupils fill the gap: 'Which ___ do you mean?'
worked_example_and_fade.situation: A worker has to sort cups. They do not know which tray to use.

adaptations.Cognition & Learning: Read one scene at a time. Model one short message and leave the frame in view. Use the same ASK, TELL and HELP words across the lesson.
adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Allow pointing, a prepared phrase, a written message or an adult scribe. Give silent thinking time. Do not demand eye contact or roleplay.
adaptations.SEMH: Use fictional scenes. Allow a watch-first route and a brief quiet pause. Keep feedback about the words used and the next step.
adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Keep scenarios as paper or screen scenes. Seat pupils where speech is clear. Offer large print and a suitable writing or pointing method.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pre-teach tray, spill, shelf and colleague with real objects or simple teacher demonstration. Rehearse one short English frame.

ta_focus.I do: Point to the question words and give wait time.
ta_focus.We do: Ask 'What does the worker need to know?' before offering a frame.
ta_focus.Independent: Use the least help needed. Record the pupil's own words and the level of support.

prompt_ladder: 1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short question. 3 Rephrase the instruction. 4 Provide a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task.

main_hinge.question: A worker is told to put a box 'there'. They do not know where. Which reply helps?

options.B: Which place do you mean, please?

main_hinge.reason: It asks for the detail the worker needs.
main_hinge.decision: If every pupil chooses B and gives or points to a useful reason, move to the route task. Otherwise re-model one question and use the parallel hinge.

parallel_hinge.question: A worker cannot hear the task. Which reply helps?

options.A: Please can you say that again?
options.B: I will do a different job.
options.C: I will walk away without telling anyone.

parallel_hinge.reason: It asks for the task again so the worker can check.

success: I can say what I need to know.
I can tell a lead worker about a problem.
I can use kind, clear words with a person at work.

evidence.description: Actual book/typed/pointed/oral response with date, work reference, access, supplied answers, first response, one NS and reply.

assessment: Record actual evidence against each outcome. Shown means evidence covers it with access logged. Partly means some parts shown. Not yet seen includes missing work or a pass; specify which. Do not count an adult model as independent work. Classroom practice is not proof of workplace competence.
private_help_route: Ask a trusted adult for a private talk. Point to HELP, write or use your aid. You may pass, pause and return with help. No personal story is needed.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Book, pointing, an aid, typing or an exact scribe are valid. Read back a scribed reply and allow a change. Record access apart from supplied answers. Plan in any language.

typed_route.heading: Type instead
typed_route.save: Use the usual save routine with lesson code and work reference; share privately.

feedback: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual evidence saved; R responded. R follows Voice and Audience, one NS and the pupil reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Add to Careers Portfolio. Offer to the Communication portfolio.
where_this_leads: clear questions and reports help people learn tasks and work with others.
colour_blind_safe: Words and card IDs carry meaning. No colour-only codes.
accreditation: Evidence may contribute to the unit award. Staff confirm actual evidence and mapping; completion is not automatic.
worked_examples_status: All workers, workplace situations and replies are invented. No employer, brand, place or private individual is named.
publication: Only Public replacements and Shared_Resources are intended for public use. Delivery publishes nothing.

Communication and asking for help
Unit: Resilience & Change — Work-ready resilience
Theme: Resilience & Change. Five teaching weeks. Week 5 is the closing lesson and brings rows 26 and 27 together. Group: up to five learners. Supported is the default.
Exact lesson outcomes
I can ask for clarification, report a problem or speak to a customer/colleague using appropriate language.
Source: BUILD Careers scheme, Spring 2 rows 24. Focus and outcomes supplied verbatim in the current brief.
Prepare and purpose

Teach useful habits with invented, unnamed workplaces. Books, pens, Support Cards, Vocabulary Mat and Evidence Sheet. Print cards as reusable references. No write-on pupil sheets, internet, login or personal phone is needed. Read the exact outcome aloud and explain the short goal.
Where this leads: clear questions and reports help people learn tasks and work with others.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So; British Values IL/MR. Respectful speech, a private choice of response and safe help-seeking are practised.
Forty minute sequence

table: Get your book. Write the date and title. Point to ASK, TELL or HELP. A worker hears: Put it over there. What could they ask?
Listen: 'Which tray do you mean?' Then: 'So these cups go on this tray. Is that right?'
Help the group ask a clear question. Help the group tell a lead worker about a spill. Choose the best words. Give one reason, or point to the clue.
In your book, choose a route. Write or say words a worker could use.
Read one answer back. Make one word or sentence more clear. A worker does not know which shelf to use. What could they ask?

blocks_in_document_order.paragraph: Teaching and checks
Arrival and retrieval 5 minutes

Show the three words ASK, TELL and HELP. Read the goal aloud. Let pupils point, say or write one word. Explain that each made-up scene is in an unnamed workplace. Pupils may watch a model instead of acting. Read: 'A worker hears: Put it over there.' Ask what the worker needs to know. Accept a short question or a point to the unclear words. Say that asking a question can help work go well.
I do 8 minutes

Model the worked example. Say the need, ask one short question, listen, then say the next step back. Model a calm tone without demanding eye contact. Show the difference between guessing and checking. Check for understanding: Which words ask where the items go?
We do 10 minutes

Use scenarios 1 and 2. Build one question and one problem report as a group. Write the exact pupil words. Model the lead worker's reply, then invite one pupil to say the safe next step. Pupils can use a voice, a card or a short book response. Use the hinge. Every pupil chooses A, B or C before discussion. If all choose B and explain that it checks the task, move on. If any pupil chooses another answer, model 'Which box do you mean?' and check again with the parallel hinge. Keep all liquids and tools as paper scenes.
You do 12 minutes

Offer Supported, Independent or Aspire cards. Pupils work in books. They may say answers for an adult to note. Keep the key goal the same across tiers. Do not require a pupil to act as a difficult customer. Use scenarios 3 and 4 for transfer. Use three brief response trials: ask for clarification, report a problem, and reply to a customer or colleague. Record the actual response and prompts for each trial.
Review and exit 5 minutes

Ask pupils to check one message: Is it kind? Is it clear? Does it say what is needed? Give one specific verbal feedback point and one next step. Invite a small edit. Do not equate a loud voice or eye contact with good communication. Read the exit scene. Accept one appropriate question. Ask the pupil to name who could help. Record the route, support and next step on the Evidence Sheet. Offer evidence to the Communication portfolio.
Model and fade
Pause and face the task. Ask: 'Which tray do you mean?' Listen or watch the lead worker show the tray. Check: 'So these cups go on this tray. Is that right?'
Change the model to boxes on a shelf. Pupils fill the gap: 'Which ___ do you mean?'

Model and card answers
All workplace cases are invented. Accept equivalent safe language. Do not require a public performance or a personal history.
Card A
Which tray do you mean?
The question checks the task before the worker starts.
Card B
Keep clear and tell the lead worker: 'There is a spill by the door. Please can you help?'
The report says what is wrong and where it is. The worker asks the right person for help.
Card C
I am not sure. I will ask someone who can help.
The reply is honest, kind and helpful.
Card D
Please can you say which box you need?
The worker checks the detail without blaming the other person.
Worked example and fade
Pause and face the task. Ask: 'Which tray do you mean?' Listen or watch the lead worker show the tray. Check: 'So these cups go on this tray. Is that right?'
Fade only answer cues; keep reading and communication access.
Judgement and safe delivery
Main hinge

A worker is told to put a box 'there'. They do not know where. Which reply helps? A: I will guess.  B: Which place do you mean, please?  C: You never tell me anything. Key B. It asks for the detail the worker needs.
Parallel hinge

A worker cannot hear the task. Which reply helps? A: Please can you say that again?  B: I will do a different job.  C: I will walk away without telling anyone. Key A. It asks for the task again so the worker can check.
If every pupil chooses B and gives or points to a useful reason, move to the route task. Otherwise re-model one question and use the parallel hinge.
What to retain

Clarification request; Problem report; Customer or colleague response. Record the actual words or selections, first attempt, work reference, usual access, supplied choices and answers, one NS and reply. Spelling and handwriting are not the target.
Common errors
Asking a question means a worker cannot do the job. Workers ask to make the task clear. Checking can help them do the job well.
A kind reply must sound loud and look straight at someone. A calm clear reply can be spoken, written or shown. Eye contact is not required.

Book, pointing, an aid, typing or an exact scribe are valid. Read back a scribed reply and allow a change. Record access apart from supplied answers. Plan in any language.

Theme: Resilience & Change. Five teaching weeks. Week 5 is the closing lesson and brings rows 26 and 27 together. Group: up to five learners. Supported is the default.
Exact lesson outcomes
I can ask for clarification, report a problem or speak to a customer/colleague using appropriate language.
Source: BUILD Careers scheme, Spring 2 rows 24. Focus and outcomes supplied verbatim in the current brief.
Prepare and purpose

Teach useful habits with invented, unnamed workplaces. Books, pens, Support Cards, Vocabulary Mat and Evidence Sheet. Print cards as reusable references. No write-on pupil sheets, internet, login or personal phone is needed. Read the exact outcome aloud and explain the short goal.
Where this leads: clear questions and reports help people learn tasks and work with others.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So; British Values IL/MR. Respectful speech, a private choice of response and safe help-seeking are practised.

blocks_in_document_order.paragraph: Teaching and checks
Arrival and retrieval 5 minutes

Show the three words ASK, TELL and HELP. Read the goal aloud. Let pupils point, say or write one word. Explain that each made-up scene is in an unnamed workplace. Pupils may watch a model instead of acting. Read: 'A worker hears: Put it over there.' Ask what the worker needs to know. Accept a short question or a point to the unclear words. Say that asking a question can help work go well.
I do 8 minutes

Model the worked example. Say the need, ask one short question, listen, then say the next step back. Model a calm tone without demanding eye contact. Show the difference between guessing and checking. Check for understanding: Which words ask where the items go?
We do 10 minutes

Use scenarios 1 and 2. Build one question and one problem report as a group. Write the exact pupil words. Model the lead worker's reply, then invite one pupil to say the safe next step. Pupils can use a voice, a card or a short book response. Use the hinge. Every pupil chooses A, B or C before discussion. If all choose B and explain that it checks the task, move on. If any pupil chooses another answer, model 'Which box do you mean?' and check again with the parallel hinge. Keep all liquids and tools as paper scenes.
You do 12 minutes

Offer Supported, Independent or Aspire cards. Pupils work in books. They may say answers for an adult to note. Keep the key goal the same across tiers. Do not require a pupil to act as a difficult customer. Use scenarios 3 and 4 for transfer. Use three brief response trials: ask for clarification, report a problem, and reply to a customer or colleague. Record the actual response and prompts for each trial.
Review and exit 5 minutes

Ask pupils to check one message: Is it kind? Is it clear? Does it say what is needed? Give one specific verbal feedback point and one next step. Invite a small edit. Do not equate a loud voice or eye contact with good communication. Read the exit scene. Accept one appropriate question. Ask the pupil to name who could help. Record the route, support and next step on the Evidence Sheet. Offer evidence to the Communication portfolio.
